I fixed the cleartext error by adding a debug-only network security config that allows plain HTTP to `10.0.2.2` and nothing else. I haven't built or run the app, so this is verified by reading the files only.

**Cause:** The debug build uses `http://10.0.2.2:8080/` (`app/build.gradle.kts:19`), but the app had no network security config. Android blocks cleartext traffic by default, so OkHttp threw `UnknownServiceException`.

**Changes:**
- `app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml` (new): a manifest overlay that merges only into the debug build and sets `android:networkSecurityConfig="@xml/network_security_config"`.
- `app/src/debug/res/xml/network_security_config.xml` (new): sets `cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"` for the domain `10.0.2.2` only.

**Choices I made:**
- I scoped the exception to the debug source set, so the release build (`https://api.shelftap.example/`) keeps the default HTTPS-only policy.
- I allowed only `10.0.2.2` rather than enabling cleartext app-wide, so other hosts stay HTTPS-only even in debug.

**Note:** Because the debug build now sends the session token over plain HTTP, this should stay limited to the local dev server.
